newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. embassy in Saudi issues security advisory.
newsitem.headline: U.S. embassy in Saudi issues security advisory.

text.p: The United States embassy in Saudi Arabia has warned Americans living in the kingdom that it continues to receive reports of possible further attacks on U.S. interests and urged them to exercise extreme caution.
The latest warning was issued on an embassy emergency telephone line and was addressed to Americans living in Saudi Arabia, where bomb blasts killed 24 Americans in the past year.
The warning, which a recording said was dated December 21, updates one issued on November 4.

The embassy said it "continues to receive unverified reports suggesting the possibility of further attacks on U.S. interests in Saudi Arabia. There have also been public statements threatening additional attacks against American military forces. Other reports are more general in nature."
It did not elaborate on the threats.

It warned the 35,000 Americans living in the desert kingdom to continue to exercise extreme caution, keep a low profile, reduce travel within the country, treat mail from unfamiliar sources with suspicion and pay particular attention to suspicious vehicles.

It said U.S. facilities "remain on high state of alert" in the kingdom and that the embassy continues "to work with the Saudi authorities for the implementation of additional measures designed to protect the security of Americans in the kingdom".
Security has been tightened in the past year at complexes housing Americans in Saudi Arabia, following the bomb attacks and continued reports of possible new attacks.

About 4,000 of the 5,700 U.S. troops in the kingdom, part of coalition forces enforcing a "no-fly zone" over southern Iraq, have relocated to a remote air base southeast of the capital Riyadh, where strict security measures have been implemented.
The November 1995 bombing at a U.S.-run military training centre in Riyadh killed seven people, including five Americans. Four Saudi nationals were beheaded for carrying out the attack.
Another attack killed 19 American servicemen when a fuel truck blew up at a complex housing U.S. military personnel in the eastern city of Khobar on June 25.
Recent U.S. media reports have alleged Saudi authorities had uncovered Iranian involvement in the June bombing. Iran has denied the allegations.
Saudi Interior Minister Prince Nayef this month described the reports as untrue and unreliable and said Saudi Arabia was close to revealing the results of its investigation.
The embassy said in this month's message the murder earlier in December of an American computer programmer and his wife at their housing compound in Riyadh was of purely criminal nature.
